author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. military said it struck a fast-moving vessel in the Caribbean Sea on Wednesday, killing three people aboard in the latest operation Washington describes as targeting drug-trafficking networks.

U.S. Southern Command said the vessel was traveling along established trafficking routes and alleged that intelligence confirmed its involvement in narcotics activity. The command did not publicly provide evidence supporting that claim or release the identities of those killed.

The action is part of a campaign of strikes on vessels in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific that began in September 2025. The military says the operations are aimed at people it calls narco-terrorists, while legal experts and human-rights organizations have questioned whether the strikes comply with international and U.S. law.

Reuters reported that more than 220 people have been killed across the campaign. Details about Wednesday’s location, the vessel’s cargo and any recovery operation were not immediately disclosed. The account is based on the military’s statement and remains subject to further verification.
dek: U.S. Southern Command said three people were killed in the latest military action against a vessel it alleged was using drug-trafficking routes.
headline: U.S. military says Caribbean vessel strike killed three
